In sides.png and attack.png the ends are flat or tapered with no claw, and the shaft is a flat bar rather than a rod. The claw is a named part, and every Valve crowbar shows it, so its absence caps M3 and the shape is wrong.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test as instructed. The four-reading test picked the asset once in four, so it is not caught twice or more.

M7.reason: The asset lies flat with its long axis horizontal, as a dropped weapon would. The brief names no front, and in first-person.png it stands up as a tall slab in front of the camera, so the facing is unclear and does not match the hand view of the game's crowbar.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. It has 10 triangles, well under the limit. The views show a closed bevelled solid with no open faces, inside-out faces or floating parts.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset is a large upright slab in the middle-left of the frame, where the game's crowbar sits low on the right, held by its grip with the claw up. The asset has no grip or claw to show how it is held, and it is not the same way round. In attack.png the slab moves out of the picture and nothing shows it parting from the hand where both are seen, so the failure is in placement, not in leaving the hands.
